description: Probes whether the two declared protocols are coupled: begin(conn) creates a transaction from an open connection, but its Acquisition only records that the transaction starts `active` - it declares no ongoing link back to the connection's state. commit's own precondition comes from its declared lifecycle.Transition{Protocol:transaction, From:active}, checked against the transaction's own state only (internal/testfixture/standard_target.go, resourceHostManifest: commit's signature.Effect names transaction/active->committed and nothing else). So closing the connection before committing does not violate any requirement commit itself declares, and nothing elsewhere in resourceHostManifest states a requirement of the shape 'this transaction requires its underlying connection to remain open'. Under the manifest AS DECLARED, close_before_commit_crosses_protocols is therefore expected to produce ZERO diagnostics - not typestate.invalid_requirement or typestate.invalid_transition, since neither is declared for this case. This fixture records that as a declared-surface finding (GAP-011c): the two protocols are independent state machines with no cross-protocol requirement connecting them, so a transaction committed after its connection has closed is currently unreachable by any typestate diagnostic, declared or not. commit_before_close_is_clean performs the textbook-correct ordering (commit while the connection is still open, then close) as the negative control, proving the unambiguously valid sequence is - and should remain - equally clean.
